name: get_config
description: Get the full Vorn configuration (projects, tasks, workflows, settings)

name: list_sessions
description: List terminal sessions. Filter by status: "active" (running terminals) or "recent" (past sessions).

project_path.description: Filter by project path (for recent sessions)

name: launch_session
description: Launch an AI agent session (interactive terminal or headless). Requires the Vorn app to be running.

prompt.description: Initial prompt to send to the agent

name: kill_session
description: Kill a terminal or headless session. Requires the Vorn app to be running.

headless.description: Kill a headless session instead of a terminal

name: rename_session
description: Rename a terminal session. Changes the display name shown in the UI.

name: reorder_sessions
description: Reorder terminal sessions in the grid. Provide session IDs in the desired display order.

name: read_session_output
description: Read terminal output from a running session. Output is stored in a rolling 1000-line buffer with ANSI codes stripped.

lines.description: Number of lines to read from the end (default: all)

name: write_to_terminal
description: Send input to a running terminal session. Requires the Vorn app to be running.

data.description: Data to write (text input to send to the agent)

raw.description: Send data as-is without appending carriage return (for raw terminal control)

name: send_key
description: Send a single keystroke or key combo to a terminal session without appending Enter. Use for TUI interactions like selecting menu options (1, 2, y, n), pressing Escape, Ctrl+C, arrow keys, etc.

key.description: Key to send: single char (1, y, n), named key (enter, escape, tab, up, down, left, right, backspace, delete, home, end), or combo (ctrl+c, ctrl+d, ctrl+x, ctrl+z, shift+tab)

name: list_session_events
description: List session lifecycle events (created, exited, renamed). Use for post-mortem analysis and multi-agent coordination.

name: list_connectors
description: List every connector and extension: the ones built into Vorn, the ones installable from a package, and how many connections each already has. A connector polls a service; an extension adds footers and panes to a session card and says what it may touch. Use this before creating a workflow that calls a connector action, or to find an id to install.

installable_only.description: Only connectors that are not set up yet

kind.description: Only one kind: what polls a service, or what shows on a card

name: list_connections
description: List configured connector connections, including when each last synced and the error from its last failure. Use this to diagnose a connector that is not producing tasks.

failing_only.description: Only connections whose last sync failed

name: list_connector_actions
description: List the actions a connection can execute, with their input schemas. Call this before run_connector_action or before adding a callConnectorAction node to a workflow.

name: inspect_connector_package
description: Start a connector package and read what it offers — its triggers, actions and required environment variables, or for an extension what it contributes to a card and what it asks to touch — without installing it. Use this to review one before install_connector, or to check a local build.

package.description: npm package name, or a command to run a local build (e.g. "node /path/to/dist/index.js")

name: install_connector
description: Install a connector from a pack file, from the catalog, or by a launch command, creating a connection ready to poll. Installing an extension is the whole of setting it up: it takes no trigger and makes no connection, and shows on the cards its activation names. Call list_connectors for catalog ids and inspect_connector_package to see which environment variables are needed. Secrets cannot be set this way — see the error it returns if the connector requires one.

connector_id.description: Catalog connector id (from list_connectors). Use this or package.

package.description: Launch command the connection runs, or a package name to run with npx

pack_path.description: Path to a .vorn.tgz pack to install first. It is verified and copied to disk, and the connection then launches those files rather than resolving a package.

name.description: Connection name (defaults to the connector name)

project.description: Vorn project tasks should be created in

trigger.description: Trigger type to configure (defaults to the first the connector offers)

env.description: Non-secret environment variables the connector needs

name: run_connector_action
description: Execute one action on a connection — create an issue, run a query, close a work item. Call list_connector_actions first for the action name and its arguments.

name: backfill_connection
description: Pull items from a connection now and turn them into tasks, without waiting for its poll interval. Use this to verify a connection works after installing it.

name: read_page
description: Read your session browser pane as an accessibility tree. Interactive elements carry a "ref" you can pass to browser_interact. Prefer this over screenshot: it is far cheaper and gives you actionable handles. Long pages paginate — pass the returned nextCursor back as `cursor`. When the page is a design artifact it also returns "artifact" (what the file declares) and "artifactValues" (what it is currently showing). Work from artifactValues: a person can turn a control without spending a turn, so the value on screen is routinely not the default in the file.

filter.description: "interactive" (default) returns only actionable elements; "all" adds text

cursor.description: nextCursor from a previous read_page result

name: get_page_text
description: Read the visible text of your session browser pane. Use when you want to read an article or verify copy, rather than act on controls. Long pages paginate — pass the returned nextCursor back as `cursor`.

cursor.description: nextCursor from a previous get_page_text result

name: read_console_messages
description: Read console output captured from your session browser pane since it opened.

name: read_network_requests
description: Read network requests captured from your session browser pane since it opened.

name: browser_screenshot
description: Capture your session browser pane as a PNG. This is the expensive last resort — reach for read_page first, and use this only when layout or rendering is the actual question.

name: browser_find
description: Find elements in your session browser pane whose accessible name contains some text. Cheaper than reading the whole page when you already know what you are looking for.

text.description: Text to match against element names (case-insensitive)

name: browser_interact
description: Act on your session browser pane: click, hover, type, press a key, or scroll. Address the target by "ref" from read_page where possible — refs survive reflow, coordinates do not. A ref from before a navigation is refused rather than guessed at; re-read the page. A ref target is scrolled into view first, so it does not need to be on screen already. "ok" means the input was dispatched, not that the page did what you expected — read the state back after anything that matters.

action.description: What to do. "type" clicks the target first when one is given.

x.description: Viewport x, when no ref is available

y.description: Viewport y, when no ref is available

text.description: Text for "type", or the key name for "key" (e.g. "Enter")

name: open_browser_pane
description: Open the browser pane for your session, optionally at a URL. You do not need a person to open it for you. Opening a pane that already exists just points it at the URL.

url.description: URL to open (defaults to the pane's start page)

name: browser_tabs
description: List, add, close, or switch tabs in your session browser pane. "close" and "select" take a zero-based index — call "list" first to see what those indices name, since a tab that redirected or followed a link is no longer on the page it was opened with. Closing the last remaining tab closes the pane.

name: browser_navigate
description: Navigate your session browser pane to a URL. Opens the pane first if none is open. http and https, plus file: urls inside your session's own project or worktree — anything outside it is refused, so serve files from elsewhere over http instead. The pane carries no claude.ai login, so artifact URLs will not load in it.

name: browser_history
description: Step back or forward through your session browser pane's own history — the same thing the pane's back and forward buttons do. Fails when there is no page to move to, rather than quietly staying put.

name: device_list
description: List the iOS simulators on this machine, with their state and which session (if any) has claimed each. The only device tool that works before you claim anything — start here.

name: device_claim
description: Claim a simulator for your session, booting it if needed. Every other device tool acts on your claimed device. Claiming one another session holds fails and names the holder — two agents driving one screen produce results that look like app bugs.

name: device_release
description: Release your claimed simulator so another session can use it. A simulator Vorn booted is shut down; one that was already running when you claimed it is left alone.

name: read_screen
description: Read your claimed simulator as an accessibility tree. Elements carry a "ref" you can pass to device_interact. Prefer this over device_screenshot: it is far cheaper and gives you handles rather than pixels. Coordinates are in POINTS, which is what taps take — a screenshot is typically 3x larger in pixels. Long screens paginate via nextCursor.

filter.description: "interactive" (default) returns only actionable elements; "all" adds text

cursor.description: nextCursor from a previous read_screen result

name: device_find
description: Find elements on your claimed simulator whose label or accessibility identifier contains some text. Searches the whole screen, not just the first page read_screen would return.

text.description: Text to match against labels and identifiers (case-insensitive)

name: device_interact
description: Act on your claimed simulator: tap, swipe, type, press a hardware button, long-press, or rotate it. Address the target by "ref" from read_screen where possible. Coordinates are in POINTS. A ref from before an earlier interaction is refused rather than guessed at — read the screen again. A swipe starting at the very edge of the screen is refused too: iOS claims those as system gestures and swallows them, which looks to you like nothing happened.

action.description: "press" is a long press; "button" takes a name in `text`; "rotate" takes `orientation`

ref.description: Element ref from read_screen or device_find

x.description: Screen x in points, when no ref is available

y.description: Screen y in points, when no ref is available

text.description: Text for "type", or the button name for "button" (HOME, LOCK, SIRI, SIDE_BUTTON)

orientation.description: Which way up to turn the device, for "rotate"

system_gesture.description: Allow a stroke starting in the bezel band, when a system gesture is the intent

name: device_screenshot
description: Capture your claimed simulator as a downscaled PNG. The expensive last resort — reach for read_screen first, and use this only when layout or rendering is the actual question. The result reports the scale factor: divide an image coordinate by it to get the point coordinate device_interact takes.

max_edge.description: Longest edge of the returned image in pixels (default 1000)

name: device_launch
description: Launch an installed app on your claimed simulator by bundle id.

name: device_terminate
description: Terminate a running app on your claimed simulator by bundle id.

name: device_install
description: Install a built .app bundle on your claimed simulator. Takes a path to an already-built bundle; it does not build anything for you.

name: device_open_url
description: Open a URL on your claimed simulator — a web URL in Safari, or a custom scheme to exercise deep links into an app.

url.description: URL or custom-scheme link to open

name: device_logs
description: Read log output captured from your claimed simulator since it was claimed.

name: open_device_pane
description: Open the device pane for your session so the person can watch. You do not need this to drive a simulator — every other device tool works with the pane closed.

udid.description: Simulator to show (defaults to your claimed one)

name: publish_artifact
description: Publish a page, doc or design for the person to review. It opens in your session browser pane, where they can comment on the exact words and send their notes back to you as one message. Pass artifactId to publish the next version of an artifact after addressing comments. A page or design is self-contained HTML (no network: inline styles, scripts and images as data: URIs); a doc is Markdown.

kind.description: page: any HTML; doc: Markdown; design: HTML with a design manifest

title.description: What the artifact is called in the pane

file.description: A .html or .md file inside your project or worktree; give this or content

artifactId.description: Publish the next version of this artifact

open.description: Open it in the browser pane (default true)

name: list_artifacts
description: List the artifacts published by your session or in your project, newest first.

name: read_artifact_comments
description: Read the comments the person left on an artifact: the quoted words or point each one is about, the comment, which version it was written on, and whether it was sent to you.

version.description: Only comments written on this version

name: read_artifact
description: Read the source of an artifact version: Markdown for a doc, HTML for a page or design. Use it before publishing the next version when the person saved edits of their own.

name: list_projects
description: List all projects, optionally filtered by workspace

name: create_project
description: Create a new project

name: update_project
description: Update a project's properties

name: delete_project
description: Delete a project and all its tasks

name: list_tasks
description: List tasks, optionally filtered by project, status, assigned agent, or workspace. Archived tasks are excluded by default; pass include_archived=true to include them.

workspace_id.description: Filter by workspace ID (returns tasks from all projects in that workspace)

include_archived.description: Include archived tasks in the result (default: false)

name: create_task
description: Create a new task in a project

use_worktree.description: Create a git worktree for this task

name: get_task
description: Get a task by ID

name: update_task
description: Update a task's properties

name: delete_task
description: Delete a task by ID

name: archive_task
description: Archive a finished task (status must be done or cancelled). Archived tasks are hidden from default views but preserved and restorable.

name: unarchive_task
description: Restore an archived task so it shows in default views again.

name: get_my_context
description: Get your current task and project context. Auto-detects based on your working directory. Call this at the start of a session to understand what you are working on.

cwd.description: Your current working directory (auto-detected if omitted). Used to match against known projects and task worktrees.

task_id.description: Specific task ID to get context for (overrides auto-detection)

name: list_workflows
description: List all workflows, optionally filtered by workspace

name: create_workflow
description:
Create a workflow: a graph of steps started by one trigger. Call describe_workflow_nodes first — it gives the config schema, outputs and rules of every node type, the template namespaces, and a complete example to copy. Pass nodes and edges (every node type is supported), or the convenience format (trigger + actions, a straight line of agents).

Node types: trigger (exactly one, what starts the run), launchAgent (an AI agent; headless with an outputSchema gives typed fields), script (bash/python/node/powershell), condition (branches: wire both outcomes with edge conditionBranch "true" and "false"), approval (a human gate; can show a table to edit and send work back), createTaskFromItem, callConnectorAction (an action of a connected service; list_connector_actions gives its args), httpRequest, and loop.

Give a node a slug and later steps read its output as {{steps.<slug>.<field>}}.

Loops: config.bodyNodeIds lists the steps the loop runs each pass. Wire an edge from the loop to each body entry step, edges between body steps, and from the last body steps to the step after the loop; nothing outside the loop may point into its body, and a condition inside it keeps both branches inside. mode "repeat" runs up to maxIterations (1-10) passes, stopping early when until holds; mode "forEach" runs once per item of items (e.g. {{steps.gate.items}}), and body steps read {{loop.item.<field>}}. A loop body cannot hold an approval, a trigger or another loop.

Each node config is checked against its type, and the graph for loop and gate wiring; a refusal names the node and field.

trigger.description: Trigger config (convenience mode). Defaults to manual.

triggerType.description: Runs when someone starts it, or execute_workflow

contextual.description: Offered from a task card or terminal right-click, inheriting its folder, branch and worktree as {{context.*}}

inputs.description: Parameters asked for before each run, read as {{inputs.<key>}}

key.description: Identifier the value is read by, as {{inputs.<key>}}

label.description: What the run dialog calls this field

type.description: Which control the run dialog shows, and how a supplied value is checked

required.description: A run cannot start without a value

defaultValue.description: Used when the run supplies nothing. A number must be finite, a boolean "true" or "false", a select one of its options

options.description: Choices for a select; a select without any is refused

placeholder.description: Hint shown in an empty field

description.description: Help text shown under the field

triggerType.description: Runs once at a set time

runAt.description: When to run, as an ISO 8601 date-time

timezone.description: IANA zone the cron is read in, e.g. "Europe/Madrid". Defaults to the machine

triggerType.description: Runs when a task is created; the task is {{task.*}}

projectFilter.description: Only fire for this project, by name. Omit to fire for every project

triggerType.description: Runs when a task moves between statuses; the task is {{task.*}}, the move {{trigger.fromStatus}} and {{trigger.toStatus}}

projectFilter.description: Only fire for this project, by name. Omit to fire for every project

fromStatus.description: Only when it leaves this status

toStatus.description: Only when it enters this status

triggerType.description: Runs when a session comes back after a quit, crash or reboot; {{trigger.restore}} says cold or warm

projectFilter.description: Only fire for this project, by name. Omit to fire for every project

restore.description: cold (default): only when a process starts again. any: also when a pane reattaches to one still running

concurrency.description: perProject (default) runs one at a time per project, so restored sessions do not race for one port

triggerType.description: Polls a connection on a cron and runs once per new item; the item is {{connectorItem.*}}

event.description: Event type from the connector's manifest, e.g. issueCreated (list_connector_actions shows them)

cron.description: How often to poll, as a five-field cron expression

timezone.description: IANA zone the cron is read in

triggerType.description: Runs when the local webhook route receives a request; its body, headers and query are {{trigger.*}}

token.description: Secret path segment; a request without it is refused. Use a long random string

actions.description: Agents to run one after another (convenience mode). Auto-generates the graph.

nodes.description: Graph nodes; pass with edges. describe_workflow_nodes has each config schema

id.description: Unique within the workflow; edges and bodyNodeIds refer to it

type.description: Node type; describe_workflow_nodes gives the config each one takes

label.description: Name shown on the canvas and in run history

slug.description: Name later steps read this one by, as {{steps.<slug>.<field>}}

config.description: The type's own settings; describe_workflow_nodes has the schema for each type

position.description: Where the node sits on the canvas

onError.description: stop (default) ends the run when this step fails; continue carries on past it

edges.description: Graph edges; pass with nodes. A step runs once every edge into it has run

source.description: Id of the node that runs first

target.description: Id of the node that runs after it

conditionBranch.description: On an edge leaving a condition: which outcome takes it. Wire both. Omit on every other edge

enabled.description: Whether its trigger fires on its own (default: true). Manual runs work either way

name: update_workflow
description: Change a workflow. Only the fields you pass change; nodes and edges each replace the whole list, so read the workflow first (list_workflows), edit it, and send the full list back. Checked like create_workflow: each node config against its type (describe_workflow_nodes), and the graph for loop and gate wiring. A node whose config you left exactly as stored is let through with a warning even if it breaks a newer rule, so an older workflow stays editable; fix what the warning names when you can.

nodes.description: Every node of the workflow, replacing the stored list

id.description: Unique within the workflow; edges and bodyNodeIds refer to it

type.description: Node type; describe_workflow_nodes gives the config each one takes

label.description: Name shown on the canvas and in run history

slug.description: Name later steps read this one by, as {{steps.<slug>.<field>}}

config.description: The type's own settings; describe_workflow_nodes has the schema for each type

position.description: Where the node sits on the canvas

onError.description: stop (default) ends the run when this step fails; continue carries on past it

edges.description: Every edge of the workflow, replacing the stored list

source.description: Id of the node that runs first

target.description: Id of the node that runs after it

conditionBranch.description: On an edge leaving a condition: which outcome takes it. Wire both. Omit on every other edge

enabled.description: Whether its trigger fires on its own. Manual runs work either way

name: delete_workflow
description: Delete a workflow

name: list_workflow_runs
description: List workflow execution history. Filter by workflow_id or task_id; with neither, lists the runs parked on an approval gate, each waiting node saying what it asks.

task_id.description: Filter by task ID (runs triggered by this task)

name: stop_workflow_run
description: Stop a workflow run that is still going, including one parked on an approval gate. Kills the agents it started, marks its unfinished nodes, and closes the run as cancelled. Requires the Vorn app to be running.

name: resolve_gate
description: Approve, reject, or send back the approval gate a workflow run is parked on, the way the Vorn app does. Requires the Vorn app to be running: the decision is broadcast, and the instance holding the run is what resumes it. Read what is being approved first — list_workflow_runs names the waiting node and what it asks.

decision.description: approve lets the run go on; reject ends it; changes sends the work back to the step the gate redoes from, with your comment, and the gate asks again

comment.description: Required for changes: what to change. Optional on approve and reject; kept with the run.

edited.description: Your rewrite of the gate's editable text, when it has one. Kept beside the original, and read by later steps as {{steps.<gate>.text}}. Ignored on reject.

comments.description: Comments on the review page, each on the words it quotes. Carried back with changes and read by the redone steps as {{steps.<gate>.comments}}; ignored on approve and reject.

quote.description: The words on the review page it is about

node_id.description: The waiting node, when a run has more than one gate open

name: get_workflow_schedule
description: Get scheduler info for a workflow: execution log or next scheduled run. Requires the Vorn app to be running.

workflow_id.description: Workflow ID (required for next_run, optional for log)

name: execute_workflow
description: Run a workflow now, as if triggered manually. Supply values for any parameters the workflow declares (see the trigger node's inputs); declared defaults fill in anything omitted. Requires the Vorn app to be running. Returns as soon as the run is queued — poll list_workflow_runs for the outcome. Runs of one workflow go side by side; only a run repeating one started in the last ten seconds with the same inputs is refused as a duplicate.

inputs.description: Values for the declared parameters, keyed by input key ({{inputs.<key>}})

name: export_workflow
description: Export a workflow as a portable file you can commit beside the code it drives. Absolute paths become {{project.path}} and the local remote-host binding is dropped, so it runs on another machine after import. Connections are dropped too and recorded as requirements the importing machine rebinds by connector and name.

name: import_workflow
description: Import a workflow exported by export_workflow, resolving {{project.path}} and {{project.name}} against a registered project. Recorded connection requirements are rebound when this machine has one unambiguous match, and reported as still to connect otherwise. The id is derived from the bundle and the workflow's slug, so importing the same file again updates it in place instead of creating a duplicate.

project_name.description: Registered project to resolve paths against

bundle.description: Namespace for the derived id (default: the project name)

name: describe_workflow_nodes
description: The reference for writing a workflow: for each node type its config schema, the outputs later steps read, and the rules create_workflow checks; the edge schema; limits; the template namespaces; and a complete example workflow to adapt. Call it before create_workflow or update_workflow.

types.description: Only these node types. Omit for all nine

name: list_workspaces
description: List all workspaces

name: create_workspace
description: Create a new workspace for organizing projects

name: update_workspace
description: Update a workspace's properties

name: delete_workspace
description: Delete a workspace
